name: Web Animations API
role: Native element.animate() with a seekable Animation.currentTime; no library needed
summary: Browser API that animates DOM and SVG elements with keyframes, timing and a document timeline. Each Animation can be paused and its currentTime set, so frames are seekable from outside, and document.getAnimations() lists every running animation, CSS ones included. Provides seekable motion without a library, labels, nesting or plugins.
use_when: Small DOM or SVG motion that must be seekable with zero dependencies
Pausing and seeking every CSS animation on a page via document.getAnimations()
Over CSS keyframes when frames are captured by setting currentTime
avoid_when: Complex choreography with labels and nesting: Anime.js timelines
Spring physics: Motion or React Spring
Canvas or WebGL content: drive it from t directly
Path morphs, text splitting or motion paths: use a free library that supports the required operation
notes: 2026-10-26: Seek-then-capture determinism was not tested; the MDN page fetched does not describe currentTime, which is assumed from the spec.
2026-11-16: The browser-capture fixture now uses paused Animation.currentTime tracks instead of the retired GSAP dependency.

assessment.rationale: Standard-track and not experimental in Chrome since 75 per MDN browser-compat-data; seeking is a core feature. Anime.js provides reusable timeline composition when several elements need orchestration.
